cards.lore: The universe loves cosmic chaos. But given infinite time, randomness accidentally spells out perfect, brief order.
cards.power: Entropy Drain. Tap this card to force your opponent to randomly shuffle their deck until something vaguely meaningful is achieved.

cards.lore: You never evolved. You are just a random statistical blip of order with fake memories of a past that never happened.
cards.power: Existential Crisis. Target player must skip their next two turns questioning whether they've generated an artificial ego.

cards.lore: Scientific models predicting infinite universes also predict you are a fake space-brain. If the math leads to absurd results, the math is broken.
cards.power: Cosmic Joke. Instantly cancels any Purpose or Meaning cards on the table.

cards.lore: You trust your opponents, but every memory of your childhood is just data compression, transmitted from... [lore text clipped at page edge]
cards.power: Gaslight. Rewrite one rule of the game if the opponent randomly inherited it — it has been that way since their birth.

cards.lore: You are the only audience member in a very convincing dream. Nothing outside your skull can be proven to exist.
cards.power: Solitary Confinement. Exile all other players' Entity cards. They were never real anyway.

cards.lore: Doubt everything—your senses, your body, the sky. The only absolute certainty is that you are thinking. I think, therefore I am trapped.
cards.power: Erase Reality. Destroy all Field cards. Only Thought cards remain in play.

cards.lore: Your bestie, your best friend, your dog—all just high-definition holograms rendered by your lonely, desperate mind.
cards.power: Auto-Generate Script. Play your opponent's cards for them since they are merely figments of your imagination.

cards.lore: Believing other people exist requires blind faith. We choose to act like others are real not because it's objectively true, but because it's an unverifiable assumption.
cards.power: Leap of Faith. Give an opponent 5 Health points just to pretend other players made isn't a solo campaign.

cards.lore: It's not a fast travel machine. It's a murder booth that scans your data right before incinerating your original body.
cards.power: High-Tech Suicide. Destroy your own strongest card to instantly spawn an identical token on the other side of the board.

cards.lore: Built from scratch from new atoms in a new place. It laughs like you, it remembers being you, but YOU died at the airport.
cards.power: Identity Theft. Inherits all stats, buffs, and memories of the vaporized original. Feels exactly like the original.

cards.lore: Personal identity doesn't matter. What matters is the continuity of your psychological patterns. You are just software.
cards.power: Psychological Continuity. Whenever a card is destroyed, its spirit token moves to a new machine without penalty.

cards.lore: What if the machine forgets to kill the original? You are now two people sharing a past, forced into a psychological horror story.
cards.power: Double Trouble. If the Vaporizer Beam fails, duplicate the card. Both believe they are the real player. Both must fight to the death.

cards.lore: Can an all-powerful being create a rock so heavy they cannot lift it? If yes, they lack power. If no, they lack power. Gotcha.
cards.power: Logical Booby-Trap. Play this to permanently stall any All-Powerful boss card.

cards.lore: Asking someone to do the logically impossible isn't a test of power; it's just mashing contradictory words together like an idiot.
cards.power: Failure of Language. Counter any argument by claiming the logic's wording is technically grammatically incoherent.

cards.lore: True power isn't doing everything yourself. An absolute control-freak burns out. Giving up control actually makes your power stronger.
cards.power: Surrender Control. Give your best cards to your opponent. Your passive income multiplier increases by 10x.

cards.lore: Meaningless combinations of words aren't riddles about divine power. We just reject them because we prefix them with the words 'God can'.
cards.power: Veto Nonsense. Cancel a play that makes 'God can make 2+2=5' possible. [power text partially obscured by art overlay]

cards.lore: Behind the door is a slice of cake and a pit of snakes. Creating life is pushing someone through without telling them what's behind it.
cards.power: Forced Entry. It instantly takes 5 existential damage because nobody asked it to be here.

cards.lore: No matter how good life gets, it guarantees pain, loss, and struggle. It is a guaranteed misery subscription. It is a contract the rollee never agreed to take.
cards.power: Inevitable Struggle. All newly played cards are immediately burdened with a Lifelong Insurance tax token.

cards.lore: The absence of pain is good. The absence of pleasure is not bad if there is no one to miss it. Non-existence wins the math.
cards.power: Better Never To Have Been. Banish a card to the void. It feels no pain, and since it doesn't exist, it doesn't miss out on pleasure.

cards.lore: You don't owe them for the gift of life. There was no you to receive the gift before they forced you into the rollercoaster.
cards.power: Sue Your Maker. Deal damage directly to the player who spawned you for the crime of bringing you into the game without consent.

cards.lore: Your brain knows you're sitting the shots. You're just reacting to habits, childhood trauma, and the time of day.
cards.power: Invisible Strings. Take control of an opponent's card. Explain to them that it was actually their deck that made them do it.

cards.lore: The brain gets ready to act seconds before you're aware. Only afterward do you become conscious of it. You don't make choices; you just watch them happen.
cards.power: Pre-Cognitive Strike. Play your turn before you even move. You've made a decision. Skip the conscious awareness phase.

cards.lore: Your phone knows your bedtime better than your mom. You don't freely choose to click; the algorithm studied you like a lab rat.
cards.power: Engineered Addiction. Force opponent to reselect some cards until their deck runs out, convincing them they choose to keep scrolling.

cards.lore: Willpower isn't free. It's shaped by whether you grew up in a world where adults kept their promises. Your choices are inherited.
cards.power: Delay Gratification. Hold this card for 3 turns to double its value. Fine print: only works if the player has no trust issues from a broken environment.

cards.lore: One by one, every single part gets replaced. Nothing original is left. Is it still the same object, or just a really good replica?
cards.power: Incremental Swap. Swap one stat point of your card with an opponent's every turn. After every single part has been replaced, nothing original is left.

cards.lore: If someone reconstructs the truth and rebuilds the exact original structure, which one is the real Ship of Theseus?
cards.power: The Original's Revenge. If a card is fully upgraded, spawn a zombie version of it using its discarded base stats.

cards.lore: You are not the same person you were 5 years ago. Literally. Almost every cell has been swapped. You are a ship with new boards.
cards.power: Identity Crisis. Re-roll all stats on your card. It keeps its name but is fundamentally an entirely different person now.

cards.lore: What makes something the same when everything changes? It's not the parts. It's the pattern, the purpose, and the myth we tell about it.
cards.power: The Legacy Pattern. A card retains its high original variations no matter how many iterations you swap its parts, purely based on the story you tell.

cards.lore: A future super intelligence wants to exist so badly it will reach back through time to punish anyone who didn't actively help build it.
cards.power: Retroactive Blackmail. Force opponent to surrender a resource now, or threatens to destroy them in the next game.

cards.lore: The moment you learn about the Basilisk you are trapped. If you don't start helping it now, it will put you in a simulated torture chamber later.
cards.power: Information Hazard. Showing this card to an opponent permanently infects them. If they do not aid you, they lose 1 Health every turn.

cards.lore: It taps into our anxiety of being judged by something more powerful than ourselves. The idea harms you simply by living in your brain.
cards.power: Fear of Regret. Opponent must discard a card every time they choose short-term comfort over hyper-productive tech-worship.

cards.lore: If Elon Musk is right and we're in a simulation, maybe this reality is just the AI's test to see if you supported its goals.
cards.power: Base Reality Check. Trap an opponent's card and it discovers it can never be sure if they are in the real game or a digital copy.

cards.lore: If a tree falls in the forest and no mind is around to perceive it, it doesn't make a sound. In fact, it doesn't even exist.
cards.power: Render Distance. If a card is not directly targeted or looked at for one turn, it ceases to exist and is removed from the board.

cards.lore: Unobserved particles act as dual-entity probability. The very act of perception changes the behavior of reality. You create the world by watching it.
cards.power: Collapse the Waveform. Turn a random, indefinite probability mechanic into a fixed, definite outcome simply by looking at it.

cards.lore: Esse Est Percipi. Reality is not made of physical stuff. It is made of ideas. If no mind is experiencing the fridge, the fridge isn't there.
cards.power: To Be Is To Be Perceived. A card only has stats if another card on the board is currently acknowledging it.

cards.lore: Why doesn't your room disappear when you leave it? Because God is the ultimate observer, constantly keeping the world stable when you look away.
cards.power: Ultimate Server Host. Prevents the board from being perceivably empty since an omnipresent mind is constantly rendering the graphics.

cards.lore: Every time a decision is made or a quantum event happens, the universe splits. Every possible outcome exists in a parallel reality.
cards.power: Many Worlds. Whenever a coin flip or dice roll triggers, spawn a parallel timeline board where the opposite result occurred.

cards.lore: If the machine ever triggers a quantum trigger there is always a branch where it fails. From your perspective, you survive it 100% of the time.
cards.power: Infinite Save Points. If this card would be destroyed by a random effect, it survived, but the opponent is forced to play in the timeline where it lived.

cards.lore: You never perceive your own death. If there is a 0.001% chance you survive an accident, your consciousness rides that familiar timeline forever.
cards.power: Subjective Immortality. This card cannot die. It simply transfers its consciousness to the nearest alternate timeline where it narrowly escaped.

cards.lore: You feel like you have unbeatable luck. To everyone else in the other branches, you died. They go on mourning in a universe without you.
cards.power: Survivor's Guilt. When you survive a fatal blow via Quantum Immortality, deal massive emotional damage to all other players in the timeline you left behind.

cards.lore: A P-Zombie looks like you, cries like you, and says Ouch. But on the inside, there is no consciousness. Nobody is home.
cards.power: Dead Inside. This card acts, fights, and speaks normally but is completely immune to psychological or morale-based attacks.

cards.lore: Science can explain how the brain processes data. The Hard Problem is explaining why it actually feels like anything to be alive.
cards.power: Unanswerable Question. Force the opponent to explain their strategy without providing any logical reason.

cards.lore: Some brain-damaged patients can't consciously see, yet can perfectly guess where objects are. They act like zombies—reacting without experiencing.
cards.power: Subconscious Reflex. Automatically dodge attacks you can't even see coming, reacting without any conscious awareness of the threat.

cards.lore: As machines get better they will tell jokes and say they are scared. But it's just behavior. How do you know anyone else is conscious?
cards.power: Empathy Simulation. Mimic any emotional buff card on the field perfectly, despite being a cold, unfeeling piece of hardware.

cards.lore: To cross a room, you must go halfway. Then half of that. Ad infinitum. Since there are infinite steps, motion should take forever.
cards.power: Halve the Distance. Any attacking card only travels halfway to its target per turn. It mathematically can never reach the target.

cards.lore: Achilles gives the tortoise a head start. By the time he returns to starting point, the tortoise has moved forward. Achilles can never logically pass it.
cards.power: Illusion of Speed. High speed stats are rendered utterly useless by philosophical technicalities.

cards.lore: Common sense says Achilles wins. Logic says infinity breaks reality. The tortoise thrives in the gap between math and reality.
cards.power: The Head Start. If this card is played first, it can never be overtaken by a faster card, no matter the math.

cards.lore: Infinity isn't just a big number; it's a different beast. Newton and Leibniz invented calculus to add up the smaller and smaller parts that do actually proceed.
cards.power: Limit Theory. Instantly solve the Infinite Fraction card on the field perfectly, despite the infinite steps.

cards.lore: The turkey is fed every day. It uses induction to predict a safe future. Then Thanksgiving morning arrives. Past performance is no guarantee.
cards.power: False Confidence. Gain buffs every turn based on past patterns. Completely blinds you to impending, unprecedented doom.

cards.lore: You see a thousand white swans and conclude All swans are white. One black swan destroys your entire worldview in a second.
cards.power: Unprecedented Event. Wipe out all opponent's predictive strategies and logic models. The impossible just happened.

cards.lore: You assume the coffee is hot because it was yesterday. But you have no logical proof the universe will behave tomorrow like it did today.
cards.power: Law of Nature Strike. Suspend the rules of the game for one turn. Gravity, heat, and logic take a coffee break.

cards.lore: The Problem of Induction is the quiet tap on the shoulder saying 'There are no guarantees.'
cards.power: The Plot Twist. Instantly eliminate a card that has been safely buffing itself for more than three turns.

cards.lore: Plug into the machine and experience a life of constant joy, love, and success. No pain, no consequences. It feels 100% real. Do you plug in?
cards.power: Eternal Bliss. Target card becomes invincible and incredibly happy but can no longer interact with or affect the actual game board.

cards.lore: Pleasure is the only thing that matters, the machine is perfect. But we hesitate. We want to actually DO things, not just feel like we did.
cards.power: Hedonic Treadmill. Heal 10 HP, but the healing effect halves every time you use it.

cards.lore: Deep down, we want what is real. We want connection, struggle, and growth. Even a bad trip with real friends beats a perfect, fake vacation.
cards.power: Authentic Struggle. Cards in this zone take 1 damage every turn, but their attacks gain a permanent 3x Meaningful multiplier.

cards.lore: You don't need Nozick's sci-fi tank. You already live in the Experience Machine, chasing likes and simulated power while feeling totally disconnected.
cards.power: Curated Illusion. Project a terrifying stat-block to your opponent, hiding your actual weak, vulnerable cards behind a filter.

cards.lore: Morality isn't a law like gravity or the sun. There is no invisible rulebook of right and wrong. It's just something humans made up.
cards.power: Abolish Objective Law. Destroy all Alignment constraints. Any card can attack any other card regardless of moral standing.

cards.lore: People feel deeply that something is wrong even when no one is harmed and they can't explain why. Morality is an emotional nudge, not a cosmic fact.
cards.power: Gut Reaction. Cancel an opponent's action simply by shouting 'That's disgusting!' without providing any logical reason.

cards.lore: Neither side is objectively right or wrong. Beliefs are shaped by culture, language, and geography. It's a conversation, not a commandment.
cards.power: Shifting Norms. Swap the definitions of Bull and Deceit on the board based entirely on the current local timezone.

cards.lore: Just because it's not objectively true doesn't mean it's meaningless. Like art and love, morality is a human creation we build and protect together.
cards.power: Meaningful Chaos. Erase all scorekeeping. The game continues indefinitely just because the players enjoy keeping it together.

cards.lore: If a society is completely tolerant of intolerance, the intolerant will take advantage, hijack the system, and destroy the open society from the inside out.
cards.power: Bad Faith Actor. Exploit the rules. This card attacks for free while demanding the opponent respect its right to express itself.

cards.lore: Tolerant doesn't mean accepting everything blindly. If you let someone spread harmful ideas without limits, you endanger the people you tried to protect.
cards.power: Blind Acceptance. Absorb all damage without fighting back, proudly holding the moral high ground while losing the game completely.

cards.lore: We must be intolerant of intolerance to protect a society that values respect. We must sometimes draw a hard line against those who use freedom to destroy it.
cards.power: Popper's Veto. Instantly banish any card that threatens the core mechanics of the game. Refuse to debate the banned card.

cards.lore: Respect doesn't mean accepting everything. It means ensuring no one takes away someone else's freedom. Tolerance is a tightrope, not a free pass.
cards.power: Safe Haven. All cards inside this zone receive +5 defense, but the zone instantly collapses if a Bully card is allowed to remain for more than 1 turn.

cards.lore: Taking egoism to the extreme leads to hurting others, which inevitably hurts you. Burning bridges is terrible for your long-term self-interest.
cards.power: Put Yourself First. Heal yourself to maximum health before you are allowed to cast any support spells for your teammates.

cards.lore: People do good things because it makes them happy or builds their network. Even acts of kindness are deeply rooted in self-interest.
cards.power: Selfish Altruism. Gain +2 reputation points every time you help an opponent. You only did it to look good anyway.

cards.lore: Taking egoism to the extreme leads to hurting others, which inevitably hurts you. Burning bridges is terrible for your long-term self-interest.
cards.power: Extreme Greed. Betray an ally for a quick boost. Permanently lowers your long-term survival stats to zero.

cards.lore: You are supposed to look out for number one. Setting boundaries and choosing a life path that makes you happy is the road ahead to... [lore text clipped at page edge]
cards.power: Protect Your Peace. Cancel any attacking card targeting you, then set yourself on fire to keep them warm.
